summary: SIEM feed s130_double is degraded: 12.3% of frames are oversized and dropped at the 1518-byte NIC, and 52.2% arrive inside ERSPAN tunnels hiding inner flows from SIEM parsing.

findings.root_cause: 396 of 3219 frames (12.3%) exceed the SIEM's 1518-byte MTU (largest 8108 bytes). Packet broker is forwarding jumbo/ERSPAN-encapsulated frames without slicing to the tool's MTU, so the SIEM NIC drops them on ingress.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM never sees 12.3% of traffic - dropped at NIC before ingestion. Complete blind spot for large flows, breaks correlation and alerting for those sessions.

recommended_fix.why: SIEM needs_full_payload=false, so slicing to 1518 preserves L2-L7 headers for detection while fitting the 1Gbps port MTU and preventing NIC drops. No full payload needed.

findings.root_cause: 1679 of 3219 frames (52.2%) arrive inside ERSPAN tunnels. Packet broker is mirroring/encapsulating traffic and forwarding it without stripping the outer ERSPAN header before delivery to the SIEM.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM sees only outer ERSPAN/IP headers and cannot parse inner original IP/TCP/application headers for 52% of traffic. Rules, parsing and correlation fail on encapsulated flows, severely reducing detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Stripping ERSPAN at the packet broker exposes the inner original packets so the SIEM can parse and correlate them natively without requiring tunnel-aware decoding.
